answer: Each fake identity must pass a spiral relay: a randomly drawn peer pair validates the submission, and the jury pays only if both relays agree. The definite cost per fake is the plume escrow posted to summon the relay, and it rises with the number of fakes because every clone competes for the same small relay pool, so each additional clone must post a higher ridge bond to outbid the last. Because one relay pair serves only one submission, k clones demand k relay slots; and because linked clones share one spiral signature trail, one failed relay poisons the whole ridge batch at once.
